articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The document "SJAA EPHEMERIS" provides a comprehensive table of astronomical data for the year 1996. It lists various celestial coordinates and parameters, including Right Ascension, Declination, Julian Date, Galactic Longitude and Latitude, Azimuth, Altitude, and True Magnitude, organized by specific dates and times. This ephemeris serves as a crucial reference for astronomers and celestial observers.

articles.title: Eye on Everything
articles.summary: The July SJAA meeting saw the approval of proposed by-laws and a presentation on Lunar Nomenclature by Bob Garfinkle. The club is actively seeking donations for a slide projector and screen, and its Observatory Committee, with $6,500 in funds, is recruiting new members. Additionally, the article announces the AANC's annual Star-B-Q in August, which includes an opportunity to observe the Perseid Meteor shower, and highlights two reviews of the new Meade ETX telescope.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document is an activities calendar outlining upcoming events for August, September, and October, primarily for the SJAA. It details general meetings, board meetings, multiple star parties at various state parks and Houge Park, an Observational Astronomy Class, and a multi-day star party trip to Mt. Lassen. Contact information for news and a home page URL are also provided.

articles.title: Meade ETX Review
articles.summary: Bill Cooke reviews the Meade ETX 90mm Maksutov telescope, noting Meade's bold marketing claims regarding its optical superiority. After a prolonged wait for his order, Cooke acquired seven units from a local Nature Company store and conducted an initial optical and mechanical inspection, uncovering some concerning issues during testing.

articles.title: ETX, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article continues a review of the Meade ETX telescope, detailing significant quality control issues observed across seven units, including optical flaws, collimation problems, and especially defective fork mount drive bases. Despite selecting the best components from multiple scopes, the author still encountered mechanical problems and design weaknesses, necessitating repairs. While capable of reasonable images for its price, the ETX suffers from highly inconsistent manufacturing quality and user-unfriendly design elements, requiring potential buyers to be prepared for extensive quality checking themselves.

articles.title: ETX Update
articles.summary: The author recounts a frustrating experience with their Meade ETX telescope's RA drive after a repair, where the promised one-minute tracking delay made it nearly impossible to keep objects centered. After 30 minutes of unsuccessful attempts, they decided not to use the drive. The author then plans to send the optical tube back to Meade due to a misaligned plastic secondary light baffle.

articles.title: By Ernie Pini
articles.summary: Ernie Pini constructed a custom binocular mount for his daughter, Elaine, to enhance her astronomical observations of Messier Objects and comets. Adapting plans from Astronomy Magazine, he implemented several design modifications for improved portability, safety, and secure attachment to a tripod. The 16-hour woodworking project, finished with Varathane, was successfully tested using Comet Hyakutake.

articles.title: By Mark Wagner
articles.summary: Mark Wagner describes a double star observing session conducted on July 2, 1996, near a full moon, as a method to enjoy astronomy despite high temperatures and light pollution. He provides a detailed log of several double stars observed using a 10-inch Dobsonian, noting that this practice helps sharpen both sky navigation and observing skills.

articles.title: Observatory Progress Report
articles.summary: Bell Dellinges provides an update on the construction of his personal observatory, "Desert Sky Observatory," in Apache Junction, Arizona. He details the progress, including the pouring of a 12'x12' slab and pier, the erection of 6' high walls, and the painting of the structure. Dellinges is currently awaiting the fabrication of the roof's wheel and track system and hopes to have the observatory operational for Fall viewing, inviting club members to visit.

articles.title: Desert Sky Observatory Completed
articles.summary: Bill Dellinges announces the completion of his Desert Sky Observatory, detailing the construction of its roll-off roof system. The roof, which weighs an estimated 1300 pounds, was built using a track system inspired by Paul Cicchetti's design, incorporating Genie garage door pulleys and angle iron tracks, allowing for easy one-handed operation. Dellinges expresses satisfaction with the new operational observatory, which now allows him to observe with his C-14 telescope without traveling to remote locations, bringing the total project cost to about $3500.

articles.title: Fremont Peak, July 7
articles.summary: Mark Wagner recounts an early morning experience at Fremont Peak where he, his daughter, and others witnessed the Space Shuttle Columbia streaking across the dawn sky. He describes the picturesque scene, with the observatory prepared for a photo and the sky ablaze with sunrise, emphasizing the profound impact the awe-inspiring event had on his eight-year-old daughter.

articles.title: Another ETX Test Drive
articles.summary: Bob Brauer provides a comprehensive review of his new Meade ETX telescope, detailing his 'test drive' experience from purchase to initial observations. While praising its good optics and portability for quick backyard observations, he highlights several manufacturing and design flaws, such as an off-center baffle, motor drive issues, and problematic tripod mounting, questioning Meade's quality control despite the scope's affordable price.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: Don Machholz reports on the discovery of Comet C/1996 N1 (Brewington) by Howard Brewington, his fifth comet, after a significant visual search effort. The article also notes the continued visibility and brightening of Comet Hale-Bopp, along with Periodic Comet Kopff, in the summer Milky Way.

articles.title: C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp)
articles.summary: This document provides ephemeris data for two comets, C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp) and 22P/Kopff, spanning from late July to late August. For each comet, it lists daily Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation, Sky quadrant, and apparent Magnitude. The data serves as a guide for tracking the celestial positions and brightness of these comets.

articles.title: C/1996 N1 (Brewington)
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for comet C/1996 N1 (Brewington) for late July and August. It lists the comet's right ascension, declination, elongation (EL), sky location (E for East), and estimated magnitude at five-day intervals.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document provides a table detailing the orbital elements for three specific comets: Hale-Bopp, Kopff, and Brewington. For each comet, it lists key astronomical parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period, along with their respective data sources. The data is presented in a clear, tabular format for quick reference.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - August 1996
articles.summary: This article presents a detailed celestial calendar for August 1996, providing essential astronomical data for observers. It includes lunar phases, rise/transit/set times, magnitudes, distances, right ascension, and declination for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The calendar also lists astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and identifies the darkest Saturday night for observation.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This article provides an update on the Telescope Loaner Program, listing the current status of various telescopes including which are available, borrowed, and their respective due dates. It also mentions a waiting list for specific telescopes and a request for donations of a tripod and German Equatorial mount to complete a newly donated optical tube assembly. The program is available to members of the SJAA, with Paul Barton as the contact.

articles.title: Thank You
articles.summary: The Astronomical Society of the Pacific's (ASP) volunteer coordinator expresses profound gratitude to club volunteers for their crucial contributions to the successful 108th annual meeting in Santa Clara, highlighting their role in creating a friendly atmosphere and smooth operation. Additionally, the article includes a call for member article submissions for the 'Ephemeris' publication and lists the current officers and Board of Directors for the club.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document, titled "Astro Ads," is a classifieds section from the August 1996 edition of the SJAA Ephemeris, featuring various astronomical equipment for sale or wanted. Items listed include Newtonian reflectors, Celestron telescopes and cameras, an Astro-Physics APO refractor, and specific accessories, with contact information for sellers and buyers. The ads are free for noncommercial astronomical products or services.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships, including standard and junior rates, and an additional fee for a Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment via check to the SJAA Treasurer, Bob Elsberry, either at a meeting or through mail. The form, dated August 1996, also lists the association's contact address and phone number.
